notes: faint pencil, read from the lower (180 degree) panel; the figures are at the limit of the scan and the day could be 6 or 18. A separate large G-like mark stands further along the same crop. Mac Dowell, played by O. E. Gorges.
pencil, read from the lower (180 degree) panel; separators dropped, as in the documented 14114 pattern, so 20 | 9 | 13

stamped, not written, and crisp; read along the roll, six figures without separators, as in the documented 311022 pattern. A second, much fainter stamp of about the same length stands beside it and is too broken to read.

region 1 carries a crisp six-position stamp running along the roll: five plain figures 9 6 1 2 8 preceded by a mark of two short parallel dashes, which may be an under-inked figure. The spacing is even, so no figure is missing, and the string does not parse as a day-month-year date under the conventions used here, so I have not made one of it. Region 2 carries a pencil number read as 3084, the last figure possibly 7, which I take to be the roll number; region 3 is blank paper.
Stamped; every figure plain. A further stamped mark to the right is cut by the crop edge.

All three crops searched, no writing. Crop 1 is the scanning rig rather than the roll: colour target, scale bar and the leader strap with its eyelet. Crop 2 is the join of the cloth leader to the paper. Crop 3 is plain paper with one small dark speck.

Pencil, treble edge, at the tail of the roll. Five figures, very faint and cut along their tops by the crop edge. The last is the barred 7 of these hands and the one before it a 2, giving the year 27; the middle figure matches the 5 of the roll number written at the head of the roll (crop 3), giving May; the fourth-from-last is a 2, so the day ends in 2, but its first figure is illegible and I have not guessed it. Crop 4 shows the printed leader label, WELTE-MIGNON No. 3045, Debussy Preludes, M. Welte & Soehne Freiburg i. B., with a signature in the "Played by" box; it carries no date. Crop 2 is a damp stain.
Pencil, treble edge, five figures without separators. Two plain carets for the 1s, a closed double loop for the 8, and two matching 2s.

Pencil on buff paper, five figures without separators. The 7 carries the crossbar; the two 2s match each other. The second figure is the two-lobed 8 of these hands, which read as a 6 would make the day 16.

All three crops searched, no writing. Crop 1 is a round stain, crop 2 perforations with a small dark fleck, crop 3 the join of the cloth leader to the paper with a printed English instruction slip, cut by the crop edge and carrying no date.
All three crops searched, no writing. Crop 1 has faint smudges only, which enhancement shows to be paper grain and staining; crops 2 and 3 are perforations with a dark repair patch.

Pencil, treble edge. Six figures grouped 2 + 2 + 2, all of them cut along the top by the crop edge, which begins at the first row of ink. The last two are the same figure, a hooked top with a diagonal and a base, giving the year 22; the middle pair are a plain diagonal and an oval, giving the month 10; the first is a 2. The second figure shows two lobes and looks like the open-topped 8, which would make the day 28, but it is not legible enough to fix and I have not completed it. Crops 2 to 4 carry only a repair patch and stains.
All four crops searched, no writing. Each shows perforations with translucent repair patches over them, and crop 4 a small dark fleck.

Pencil, treble edge, at the tail of the roll. Five small figures, about 27 px each, cut along the top by the crop edge. The last two are secure: the 2 matches the 2 of the roll number written at the head of the roll (crop 4) and the 1 is a plain stroke, so the year is 21. My best reading of the rest is 30 and 8, giving 30 August, but the first figure could be a 2 (day 20) and the third could be a 6 (June), so I have left date_iso at the year alone rather than complete it. Crop 2 carries a short pencil tick, crop 3 creases, crop 5 the leader join.
